title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 4
paragraphs: At this time, however, even these Greeks who had come to Artemisium, when they saw that a great number of ships had put in at Aphetai and the whole area was filled with the enemy's armament, were struck with fear — for the barbarians' fortunes had turned out differently from what they expected — and they deliberated about retreating from Artemisium into the inner parts of Greece. When the Euboeans realized what they were considering, they asked Eurybiades to stay there with them for a short time, until they could remove their children and households from the land. When they failed to persuade him, they went elsewhere and persuaded Themistocles, the Athenian commander, by a payment of thirty talents, on condition that the fleet should stay and fight the sea-battle in front of Euboea.
